items.title: Warhammer 40,000 Animated Series Produced by Henry Cavill to Tell a 'Long-Form Story' Featuring The Deathwatch
items.description: The Warhammer 40,000 animated series in development by Amazon will tell a "long-form story" featuring The Deathwatch, with Henry Cavill set to serve as an executive producer.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
The Warhammer 40,000 animated series in development by Amazon will tell a "long-form story" featuring The Deathwatch, with Henry Cavill set to serve as an executive producer.

The series will begin as a spinoff from the Warhammer 40,000 episode of Secret Level, Amazon's animated anthology series that aired back in 2024, Amazon announced previously. The episode's director Dave Wilson will now serve as this new series' director and co-creator, alongside Band of Brothers writer John Orloff. Animation will once again be handled by Blur Studios.

This is on top of a further Warhammer episode of Secret Level set to debut in the series' upcoming second season, though set in the Warhammer: Age of Sigmar universe.

Details of what Amazon's full animated series will feature remain thin on the ground, other than it starring elite alien-hunting Space Marine group The Deathwatch. Exactly how many episodes the series will feature remains to be seen, though Wilson has described the project as a "long-form story" set in the Warhammer 40,000 universe.

"Secret Level wasn't conceived simply as an anthology," Wilson told Variety. "It was designed as a launchpad for larger stories. The response to the Warhammer episode was extraordinary, particularly from fans who understood how much care went into getting the world right.

"This series gives us the opportunity to build on that foundation and tell a much larger story. I've wanted to tell a long-form story set in Warhammer 40,000 for more than 20 years, and I'm incredibly grateful to Games Workshop and Amazon MGM Studios for the opportunity to do it."

Warhammer 40,000 is already set to become a live-action series, with Amazon and Cavill still working on that. Indeed, we recently learned that horror maestro Mike Flanagan is now on board the project too. But with a script for that still to be written, there's a possibility that this new project may end up debuting first.

Amazon's other game-related projects include its Fallout series, upcoming Tomb Raider show starring Game of Thrones' Sophie Turner, a God of War series that's currently going through some cast changes, and a Life of Strange adaptation that is currently filming.

Image credit: YouTube

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Rust Fan Sues Police After Swatting Incident Leaves Him Paralyzed
items.description: A Rust player left paralyzed by cops in a swatting incident is now suing the police for $176 million.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
A Rust player left paralyzed by cops in a swatting incident is now suing the police for $176 million.

Back in April of this year, 23-year-old Tucson resident Axeel Melendez was shot in his leg and spine by two officers who stormed into his house via his bedroom window. The cops were responding to a false report of an active shooter in the building — despite Melendez previously warning their unit that he was being targeted by a potential swatter.

Melendez will likely remain paralyzed from the waist down for the rest of his life, and is now seeking damages for his medical expenses and wage losses.

Just two days before, Melendez had been hacked by another player of the survival game Rust, who accessed personal details on his computer and then demanded money not to release them publicly. Melendez didn't pay, and was then threatened with swatting — a practice where armed law enforcement is called to an address under false pretences.

Concerned for his safety, Melendez called 911 to report the threats and alert cops that his address could be swatted.

"They said that they were going to call the police station and say that I have a bomb so that FBI shows up at my house so I could get swatted," Melendez told a 911 responder, in a tape of the call reported by the Arizona Daily Star. "They knew my ethnicity, so they said that they were going to call ICE to show up at my house and get my whole family deported. We're all citizens, so it's okay."

In response, Melendez was told that a hoax caller "can't just call the SWAT on you" and that "nothing is going to happen."

An officer even visited Melendez's house to offer further reassurance, and state that deputies had been informed to be aware of fake emergency calls regarding his address. Regardless, just two days later, cops responded to a report that Melendez's father had shot his sister, and stormed the house with guns drawn.

Police video of the incident released into the public domain shows officers shouting from outside the house that they are from the sheriff's department, before giving up and using a shovel to smash Melendez's bedroom window. Seeing the end of Melendez's shotgun being pointed in their direction from behind a door, the officers open fire.

Melendez has said he was wearing noise-cancelling headphones to play games when the cops were outside, and only realized that someone was entering the house when his window was smashed. He then ran to wake his sleeping mother, and grabbed the family's legally-owned gun.

"My goal was to get some experience working on highline cars and then more advanced education in automotive engineering," Melendez said, reflecting on his life before he was paralyzed. "I really wanted to work on an F1 engineering team. I love soccer, and I enjoy reading and board games. I liked to be active and do stuff outside."

Local police have declined to comment on the matter further.

Swatting has sadly become a relatively common practice, and numerous video game fans who play or stream online have fallen victim. Grand Theft Auto 5 actor Ned Luke has been targeted numerous times, and recently celebrated one swatter finally receiving jail time.

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Almost Featured a Bizarre, Sticky Marvel Supervillain
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton has revealed a sticky Marvel supervillain who was originally set to feature in the movie.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton has revealed a sticky Marvel supervillain who was originally set to feature in the movie.

Cretton planned for Marvel's classic glue-shooting baddie Paste-Pot Pete to appear as part of the movie's introductory montage. It's here we see Spidey fighting villains such as Scorpion, Boomerang and Tombstone — and it's clear that more enemies were once planned.

One of these enemies would have been Peter Petruski, better known as Paste-Pot Pete, who first debuted in Marvel comics back in 1962. Created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby, the character has tangled with Spider-Man and the Fantastic Four over the years, and briefly been a part of teams such as the Frightful Four and the Sinister Six.

Here is Paste-Pot Pete:

How are we getting things like Aquaman 2 and El Muerto before we get what fans really want? Paste Pot Pete: The Movie. pic.twitter.com/gD4cZixsVL

— Comic Tropes (@CTropes) April 27, 2022

In terms of his abilities, Pete shares some similarity to Tom Holland's Spider-Man by firing a sticky adhesive (initially from a glue gun, but later from wrist-mounted devices), allowing him to shoot ropes and webs, and walk on walls. It remains to be seen how well he would have matched up to Holland himself — particularly as the latter's organic web skills develop.

"We played around with a lot of villains who didn't make it into the final cut in the end," Cretton told OutNow. "We looked at the different [comic book] covers and considered which ones could help us tell our story.

"We wanted to show how Spider-Man cleans up the city, meaning beating up enemies. But on many covers, Spider-Man is currently getting a beating himself - so for the most part, we couldn't use those. Many classic Spidey pose covers were also unusable for us. One character we had a lot of fun with and wanted to include in the film was Pace Pop Pete - but he didn't quite make it in."

Still, perhaps there's hope for Paste-Pot Pete in Spider-Man 5? While Tom Holland's return has not been formally announced by Marvel, his future seems secure following Brand New Day's record-breaking opening weekend in theaters that brought in an astonishing $927 million worldwide.

"Spider-Man: Brand New Day sees Destin Daniel Cretton effectively refocus on the sturdiest pillars of the webslinger's iconography: struggling to find balance while swinging around New York City saving the day, and looking dang cool doing it," we wrote in IGN's Spider-Man: Brand New Day review, which returned a 7/10 score. Maybe with Paste-Pot Pete, it could have better stuck the landing?

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

media:description.$text:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day (July 31, 2026)

Tom Holland is donning the red and blue tights once again for a fourth live-action Spider-Man movie set in the MCU. The sequel began filming in Summer 2025 for a July 2026 release. Shang-Chi's Destin Daniel Cretton is directing this time around. Heading into production, Holland teased that the latest script "really lit a fire in me," and the Brand New Day teaser trailer that hit in March, 2026, did the same for fans.

As for future solo films, during Spider-Man: No Way Home's press tour, producer Amy Pascal said that the thinking is that there will be at least three more Spider-Man films starring Tom Holland. If this pans out, Brand New Day would be the first installment in a new trilogy.

items.title: 'Final Nail in the Coffin': Xbox Price Rises Revealed, Leaving Fans Stunned as Series X/S Spike By More Than a Third in Europe
items.description: Microsoft has increased the price of its consoles by more than a third in Europe, leaving fans stunned at how much an Xbox Series X/S now costs.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Microsoft has increased the price of its consoles by more than a third in Europe, leaving fans stunned at how much an Xbox Series X/S now costs.

While these price rises are not a surprise — Microsoft announced they were coming back in June — the exact pricing for Xbox Series X and S in mainland Europe and the UK remained under wraps until now.

In the U.S., Microsoft previously stated that the 512GB Series S would rise by $100, while 1TB Series models would rise by $150 — increases that equate to around £74 and £111. The 2TB model will be discontinued completely, meanwhile — presumably because it would have become too expensive to be worthwhile making.

But in the UK and mainland Europe, the actual price rises in pounds and euros are much steeper. The 512GB Series S has jumped from £299 to £429, an increase of £130, while its 1TB model has increased from £349 to £519, a leap of £170.

Worse still are the increases for Series X models, with the 1TB Digital up from £449 to £619 (£170), but the 1TB Disc model up from £449 to £669 — whopping 48% increase, and £220 difference.

Fans have slammed the huge changes, which are far higher than expected. "Final nail in the coffin," wrote one user on the video game forum ResetEra. "Great strategy, that'll definitely lead to more sales," said another. "There is no way in 2026 I would be paying nearly £700 for a Series X with a disc drive," wrote a third.

"Still trying to process how a console that was sold for €499 almost six years ago is now €799," noted another fan. "The Series S 1TB is now €100 more expensive than the Series X at launch. This is just mindblowing."

U.S.

  • Xbox Series S (512GB) – $499.99 (was $399.99)
  • Xbox Series S (1TB) – $599.99 (was $449.99)
  • Xbox Series X (1TB, Digital) – $749.99 (was $599.99)
  • Xbox Series X (1TB, Disc) – $799.99 (was $649.99)

U.K.

  • Xbox Series S (512GB) – £429.99 (was £299.99)
  • Xbox Series S (1TB) – £519.99 (was £349.99)
  • Xbox Series X (1TB, Digital) – £619.99 (was £449.99)
  • Xbox Series X (1TB, Disc) – £669.99 (was £499.99)

Europe

  • Xbox Series S (512GB) – €499.99 (was €349.99)
  • Xbox Series S (1TB) – €599.99 (was €399.99)
  • Xbox Series X (1TB, Digital) – €749.99 (was €549.99)
  • Xbox Series X (1TB, Disc) – €799.99 (was €599.99)

Back in June, Microsoft blamed this latest set of price rises as the result of console storage and memory prices having "increased by more than 2.5x," with another "doubling by the fall of 2027" expected.

"The entire consumer electronics industry is struggling with the current components crisis, but the effects are particularly hard on consoles," Microsoft wrote. Unlike phones, computers, speakers, and other consumer devices, consoles are typically not sold at a profit, but instead for less than they cost to make."

The anouncement of the Xbox console price rises comes ahead of the release of GTA 6 in November, which is expected to increase demand for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S significantly. However, there are concerns that neither Sony nor Microsoft will be able to meet the demand caused by the release of GTA 6, with the AI boom making it particularly hard for hardware manufacturers not only to source components, but to release products at affordable prices.

Earlier this year, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said the spiralling cost of new and existing consoles would require "radically different business models" over the coming generation. She added that the industry had "reached a point where it will be hard to imagine" mass audiences still being able to afford "thousands of dollars" for a new console generation.

The current PS5 and Xbox Series X and S generation of consoles have seen price increases rather than cost savings. Sony itself raised the price of PS5 consoles back in March, blaming "continued pressures in the global economic landscape." Nintendo has also not been immune, and recently acknowledged it would up the price of Switch 2, just over a year after its arrival. And Valve has bemoaned its struggle to release Steam Machine at the price it had initially hoped, instead having to go for an eye-watering $1,049.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: As Fans Criticize Disney Fumbling Wonder Man and Blade, Creator Acknowledges 'Important Conversations' About 'The Kind of Stories We're Prioritizing'
items.description: Wonder Man creator Andrew Guest has acknowledged the "important conversations" that fans are having following word of the show's cancellation, and after Blade star Mahershala Ali slammed Disney for fumbling Blade.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Wonder Man creator Andrew Guest has acknowledged the "important conversations" that fans are having following word of the show's cancellation, and after Blade star Mahershala Ali slammed Disney for fumbling Blade.

Last week, Marvel fans were left stunned by Marvel's abrupt U-turn on a second season for the Emmy-nominated Wonder Man, which had previously been announced as renewed. Days later, Ali voiced his strongest criticism yet over Marvel's failure to make his long-promised Blade reboot, which now looks unlikely to ever happen.

While both of these projects were scrapped for separate reasons, Marvel fans have highlighted the current situaton as a "terrible look" for the company's support of projects starring Black actors, and called for better care to be taken going forward.

"Between this and Wonder Man, TERRIBLE look Marvel," one fan wrote in a lengthy thread on reddit. "Oof this really hurts," said another. "Marvel has to get their s*** together," wrote a third.

Numerous comments have highlighted the varying issues impacting the quality or release of other projects featuring Black characters in recent years. Announced in 2020, the Don Cheadle-starring Armor Wars has been left missing in action. After finishing filming in 2022, Ironheart's launch was held back until 2025, impacting the series' momentum. Samuel L. Jackson's Secret Invasion series saw Nick Fury get a solo project after 15 years, only for it to turn out as one of the lowest-rated Marvel projects ever, with no plans announced for his return. After earning Captain America's shield in 2019, Anthony Mackie's six-year wait for a movie ended in the messy and disappointing Brave New World, while some fans have criticized the subsequent reintroduction of Steve Rogers. And after crossing over to the X-Men universe at the end of The Marvels, Monica Rambeau has, so far, been left out of the Avengers: Doomsday marketing.

Of course, other Marvel projects have also hit issues or been poorly-received — both Thor: Love & Thunder and Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania quickly spring to mind — but, again, fans have pointed to the above list being an unfortunate look — and Guest appeared to agree.

"I've been listening, I appreciate you all, I feel how you all feel," Guest said in a video posted on TikTok.

"I appreciate everyone getting out there and letting your voices be heard about how you feel about this," he continued. "I think there's important conversations being had online about the kind of stories we're prioritizing and the kind of shows that platforms want to make."

Looking to the future, it's unclear to what extent Marvel still plans to make live-action Disney+ shows. Other than Vision Quest and Daredevil: Born Again Season 3, which have already been filmed, no other projects have been announced. The same is also true of Disney's Star Wars wing, which also has no confirmed further series in the pipeline now it has finished filming Ahsoka Season 2.

As for Marvel's movie projects, the company has Black Panther 3 and the Ryan Gosling-starring Ghost Rider coming in 2028 following Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars. Marvel has reserved a third 2028 release date, too, which is likely when the company's X-Men reboot will arrive.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

Announced in 2020, the Don Cheadle-starring Armor Wars has been left missing in action. After finishing filming in 2022, Ironheart's launch was held back until 2025, impacting the series' momentum. Samuel L. Jackson's Secret Invasion series saw Nick Fury get a solo project after 15 years, only for it to turn out as one of the lowest-rated Marvel projects ever, with no plans announced for his return. After earning Captain America's shield in 2019, Anthony Mackie's six-year wait for a movie ended in the messy and disappointing Brave New World, while some fans have criticized the subsequent reintroduction of Steve Rogers. And after crossing over to the X-Men universe at the end of The Marvels, Monica Rambeau has, so far, been left out of the Avengers: Doomsday marketing.

Of course, other Marvel projects have also hit issues or been poorly-received — both Thor: Love & Thunder and Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania quickly spring to mind — but, again, fans have pointed to the above list being an unfortunate look — and Guest appeared to agree.

"I've been listening, I appreciate you all, I feel how you all feel," Guest said in a video posted on TikTok.

"I appreciate everyone getting out there and letting your voices be heard about how you feel about this," he continued. "I think there's important conversations being had online about the kind of stories we're prioritizing and the kind of shows that platforms want to make."

Looking to the future, it's unclear to what extent Marvel still plans to make live-action Disney+ shows. Other than Vision Quest and Daredevil: Born Again Season 3, which have already been filmed, no other projects have been announced. The same is also true of Disney's Star Wars wing, which also has no confirmed further series in the pipeline now it has finished filming Ahsoka Season 2.

As for Marvel's movie projects, the company has Black Panther 3 and the Ryan Gosling-starring Ghost Rider coming in 2028 following Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars. Marvel has reserved a third 2028 release date, too, which is likely when the company's X-Men reboot will arrive.

items.title: Marvel's Wolverine ESRB Rating Promises 'a Handful of Sequences' Featuring 'Exposed Buttocks'
items.description: Marvel's Wolverine will have gore, intense violence, strong language, and at least a few scenes featuring "a character's exposed buttocks," according to its Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB) rating.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Marvel's Wolverine will have gore, intense violence, strong language, and at least a few scenes featuring "a character's exposed buttocks," according to its Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB) rating.

The full description for Insomniac Games' M-rated superhero experience warned would-be players that "partial nudity" is one of the many elements they'll need to consider before picking up a copy this September (via MP1st). However, a more specific explanation toward the end of the page suggested the only example of this in the game might be one or two instances of on-screen butts.

The warning reads as follows: "A handful of sequences briefly depict a character's exposed buttocks."

The context and character butt in question remains to be seen, but fans may want to prepare for Logan's rear end to be front and center in his own video game. For some reason, this isn't quite uncharted territory for Wolverine.

Disney+ left Hugh Jackman's butt uncensored when X-Men: Days of Future Past came to the streaming service back in 2020. Deadpool & Wolverine then put the focus on Jackman's behind when it came out in 2024 and allegedly nearly doubled down on it by referring to his butt as "Canada's Ass" in one deleted scene.

It's also a shame Marvel's Wolverine will be PlayStation 5 exclusive when it launches next month, as some might remember a few lucky Xbox fans got some…unique controllers a few years back. The Xbox-exclusive "designed by Deadpool" controllers both came suited up in Deadpool & Wolverine's red and yellow superhero suit attire. They also happened to be extremely caked up.

The full ESRB description for Marvel's Wolverine can be found here: "Marvel's Wolverine is rated M for Mature 17+ by the ESRB with Blood and Gore, Drug Reference, Intense Violence, Partial Nudity, and Strong Language. Also includes In-Game Purchases. This is an action game in which players assume the role of James Logan/Wolverine, as he reunites with Team X to stop a dangerous threat. From a third-person perspective, players use melee attacks and special skills to kill enemy soldiers and robots in frenetic combat. Players use their claws to slash, stab, and slice enemies; rage modes allow players to enact faster, more destructive combos and slow-motion finishers (e.g., dramatically stabbing an enemy in the head). Combat is highlighted by frequent blood-splatter effects, screams of pain, and dismemberment/decapitation. Battlefields are sometimes strewn with torsos and limbs; cutscenes can also depict blood and gore (e.g., characters tearing enemies apart, decapitating enemy soldiers). A handful of sequences briefly depict a character's exposed buttocks. The dialogue references drugs (e.g., “It doubled my production of fentanyl.”). The words “f**k” and “sh*t” appear in the game."

We didn't really need the full ESRB description to tell us that Marvel's Wolverine will veer in a new direction for the Marvel's Spider-Man game developers at Insomniac. Pre-release footage for the game has so far promised an especially gory take on the classic comic book X-Men member, with gameplay clips showing that players will be able to rip apart any goon that gets in their way.

Marvel's Wolverine has a September 15, 2026, release date for PS5. For more, you can read IGN's interview with Insomniac from June. You can also check out everything revealed in the game's "Ain't No Hero" trailer and why some fans filled up its comment sections.

items.title: Wonder Man Showrunner Confirms 'Contracts Were Signed, Schedules Were Cleared' Before Marvel Canceled Season 2
items.description: Wonder Man showrunner Andrew Guest sounded off on Marvel's decision to cancel Season 2, confirming that "contracts were signed" and "schedules were cleared" before its abrupt demise.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Wonder Man showrunner Andrew Guest sounded off on Marvel's decision to cancel Season 2, confirming that "contracts were signed" and "schedules were cleared" before its abrupt demise.

Guest is one of a few members of the crew for the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) spinoff show to share his thoughts on its cancellation in the wake of the Disney+ show's sudden and unexpected end. His message to fans arrived via TikTok and held back little regarding his disappointment.

"I just want to say I've been listening," he said. "I appreciate you all. I feel how you all feel, and I just want to clear up what I can here: This is not a marketing stunt, there is no movie in the works, and [director Destin Daniel Cretton's] schedule – and no one's schedule – was an issue."

Marvel announced Wonder Man would return for Season 2 in March and then revealed it had U-turned on that decision last week, July 30. Guest clarified that he, Cretton, and stars Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Ben Kingsley "loved making the show" and "felt passionately about continuing to do it." For some reason, Marvel had other plans.

"Contracts were signed, schedules were cleared," he added. "The writers' room was supposed to start this month. The production was supposed to begin early next year, and there was a decision made internally, between Disney and Marvel, that this didn't make sense for them, even though, a few months ago, it did.

"And that's, essentially, all I really know. Numbers aren't really shared with me."

Guest added that the first episode of Wonder Man Season 2 had been completed and an outline for the remainder of the season had been drafted before Marvel canceled it. We may never know how Simon Williams and Trevor Slattery's stories would have grown with another batch of episodes, but the showrunner said "everyone felt really good about" the now-canceled season.

Guest suggested the Wonder Man crew was just as shocked to learn about the project's end as the fans were, but it doesn't sound like they had much of a heads-up either. Arian Moayed, who reprised his MCU role as Agent Cleary for the show, chimed in on the discourse surrounding the cancellation with a statement on Instagram. Posted Friday, July 31, he said, "we all heard about the news last week."

"We are all pretty gutted by the news mostly because Wonder Man is a beautiful show, full of beautiful performances and led by beautiful writing," Moayed said. "Our show runner, Andrew Guest, made something so pure and funny and heartwarming with his scalpel-esque writing that I hope it’s studied and celebrated for years to come."

Wonder Man may not have garnered the eyes necessary to warrant a second season from Disney and Marvel's perspective, but social media feeds following its demise have been filled by fans who thought otherwise – and it's easy to see why. Those who did watch the show generally really enjoyed it, with its first season scoring a 91% critic score and 87% audience score on review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes' website. IGN gave Season 1 an 8/10 review, calling it a "a smaller, low-stakes MCU adventure that thrives on the strength of Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Ben Kingsley’s performances."

@andrewgst #wonderman #marvel #season2 #marvelwonderman #mcu ♬ Monologues - Joel P West

Abdul-Mateen was one of the first to share his thoughts on the end of Wonder Man, thanking fans with his own Instagram post. Guest had shared thoughts earlier in the week, too, but used his TikTok video as an opportunity to elaborate.

"I appreciate everybody getting out there and letting your voices be heard about how you feel about this," he continued. "I think there's important conversations being had online about the kind of stories that we're prioritizing and the kind of shows platforms want to make."

Guest signed off, saying he hopes Emmy voters are keeping Abdul-Mateen in mind come awards season. The actor was nominated for Lead Actor in a Comedy Series for the 2026 show.

items.title: Wicked Star Ariana Grande to Take a 'Step Back From Visibility' Amid 'Endless, Ongoing Public Scrutiny'
items.description: Wicked star Ariana Grande will take a ‘step back from visibility’ following her Eternal Sunshine tour, and has exited West End musical Sunday in the Park with George, which was due to open in London next summer.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Wicked star Ariana Grande will take a ‘step back from visibility’ following her Eternal Sunshine tour, and has exited West End musical Sunday in the Park with George, which was due to open in London next summer.

After her Eternal Sunshine tour wraps up in London on September 1, the superstar singer and actor will take a break from public-facing work and appearances, which, a representative told People, “has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny.” The news comes amid ongoing speculation around Grande’s body and health, including weight loss.

Here’s the statement:

“Ariana will be taking a step back from visibility after she completes the Eternal Sunshine Tour. She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny. This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much.”

Grande, who played Glinda in the Hollywood adaptations of Wicked across two films, has faced scrutiny surrounding her weight for some time. That scrutiny intensified following the release of her music video for Petal late last month. Mods for one reddit thread posting of the music video confirmed they had to remove 'incredibly disrespectful' comments about Grande's appearance. Many of the over 52,000 comments on the video on Grande's YouTube channel are about her appearance.

Grande is set to star in Meet the Parents sequel Focker-in-Law this November. It is unclear if she will promote the movie ahead of its release in theaters. She was due to appear in Sunday in the Park with George alongside Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey, who played Fiyero Tigelaar. This evening, the official X / Twitter account of Sunday in the Park with George confirmed Grande's exit.

"Following this evening's announcement from Ariana Grande's team, we can confirm that she has decided to step back from Sunday in the Park with George," the statement from the production read. "We know this cannot have been an easy decision, and she makes it with our complete understanding and support. We wish her nothing but the best. The production will open at the Barbican in summer 2027 as planned, and casting will be announced in due course."

The Wicked film series has earned massive box office success, grossing a combined total of over $1.3 billion globally across both parts distributed by Universal Pictures. Wicked came out in 2024 and involved a sweeping promotional tour alongside her co-star Cynthia Erivo, who played Elphaba Thropp. Wicked: For Good followed in 2025 and, likewise, saw Grande make repeated public appearances while promoting the movie.

After Focker-in-Law, the Grammy winner will appear in the animated adaptation of Dr. Seuss’ beloved children’s book Oh, the Places You’ll Go!," which is due out March 17, 2028. In her announcement shared to Instagram in July 2025, Grande posed in the voice recording studio alongside costar Josh Gad. Wicked director Jon M. Chu will helm the movie alongside co-director Jill Culton.

items.title: Tom Holland Says Spider-Man 5 Is 'Unclear,' Teases He Knows When Miles Morales Will Join the MCU
items.description: Details regarding Spider-Man 5 are "unclear," according to Tom Holland, but the longtime Peter Parker actor has at least confirmed he knows when Miles Morales will join the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Details regarding Spider-Man 5 are "unclear," according to Tom Holland, but the longtime Peter Parker actor has at least confirmed he knows when Miles Morales will join the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).

The infamously leak-prone actor let a few details slip when promoting his new film, Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Although he was able to keep most of his cards to his chest, he couldn't help but bring up the topic on millions of Marvel fans' minds: Miles Morales.

Holland immediately turned the conversation toward the fan-favorite Web-Slinger when asked, as a Spider-Man fan, what questions he had on his mind during an interview with 1Live. Was he willing to share a concrete answer regarding when Miles Morales will join the MCU? Well, no, but it sounds like things are moving quickly at Marvel.

"What would be the first question?" Holland pondered. "I guess it would be, 'When will we get Miles Morales?' would be the question I would ask – because I know the answer."

When asked to elaborate by the interviewer, Holland said with a smile, "I'm asking the questions. I'm not answering them."

The Spider-Man character has slipped past the MCU thus far, with Sony mostly keeping him locked away to the still-beloved Spider-Verse movies when it comes to his presence in feature films for the last decade. Holland said he had been working to bring Miles Morales into the MCU in June, and a few weeks ago, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige teased that the character likely wouldn't join his cinematic universe until sometime after the Spider-Verse saga ended.

It sounds Marvel has at least enough of a plan to share with its current Spidey star when it comes to bringing live-action Miles Morales to life, but does that mean plans for Spider-Man 5 have been ironed out? Not exactly.

Both Holland, as well as his partner and Spider-Man: Brand New Day co-star, Zendaya, spoke about the future as part of a video with Serieously that was published two days before the film's July 31 premiere. Here, the question was a bit more direct, asking Holland if he would come back for a fifth Spider-Man movie should the opportunity arise. Holland said "we would love to" while refraining from getting too into detail.

"What is on the cards is a little unclear right now, but I'm sure that, whatever happens with Spider-Man, it'll be very bright and lovely."

Zendaya chimed in: "It'll be great no matter what. We'll be sure of it."

Spider-Man 5 has not been announced by Marvel Studios or Sony, but it would be a shock to see the story stop with Spider-Man: Brand New Day. The film is currently wrapping up a record-breaking opening weekend in theaters after it brought in an estimated $927 million worldwide. Should a fifth film deliver the right story and cast, it's easy to see a path where the classic comic book character continues to rake in impressive numbers.

For now, audiences are probably happy with the film they have now, rather than a new one, which could be many, many years away. IGN gave the latest MCU picture a 7/10 review. Next up for the MCU is Avengers: Doomsday, which is set to premiere December 18, 2026. For more, you can read about what Feige had to say about the chances of Peter Parker meeting Venom in the MCU.

Tom Holland is donning the red and blue tights once again for a fourth live-action Spider-Man movie set in the MCU. The sequel began filming in Summer 2025 for a July 2026 release. Shang-Chi's Destin Daniel Cretton is directing this time around. Heading into production, Holland teased that the latest script "really lit a fire in me," and the Brand New Day teaser trailer that hit in March, 2026, did the same for fans.

As for future solo films, during Spider-Man: No Way Home's press tour, producer Amy Pascal said that the thinking is that there will be at least three more Spider-Man films starring Tom Holland. If this pans out, Brand New Day would be the first installment in a new trilogy.

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Comes Close to Passing Avengers: Endgame With Second Biggest Box Office Debut of All Time at $927 Million Globally
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day combined the power of Tom Holland and the MCU to bring in an estimated $927 million at the global box office during its opening weekend in theaters.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day combined the power of Tom Holland and the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) to bring in an estimated $927 million at the global box office during its opening weekend in theaters.

It's a figure that firmly places the Destin Daniel Cretton-directed superhero movie toward the top of even high-end expectations going into its July 31 premiere. Although these estimations still fell short of records broken by Marvel's Avengers: Endgame in 2019, Spider-Man: Brand New Day will comfortably swing away from its debut with the biggest opening of the year so far.

Let's break down the numbers. Domestically, the MCU Spidey flick brought in an estimated $355 million from its 4,487 theaters, with its international total sitting at $572 million. The broken records that come with that include the biggest opening ever for a Sony or Spider-Man movie, but it does still fall short of what Endgame was able to bring in.

The MCU team-up film opened to $357.1 million domestically – a painful $2 million more than Spider-Man: Brand New Day – and an unbelievable $1.2 billion globally. Although Holland, who appears in both films, comes out a winner either way, the new Spider-Man movie does still come in second on both accounts – but there is a catch.

The box office calculations we're seeing today are the estimates for the weekend as final totals for Sunday are tallied. Although Endgame’s spot globally seems secure, the domestic race is brutally close. A small bump could potentially see Spidey take the domestic crown as the count is ironed out in the coming days. Regardless, it won't be all second-place victories for Spider-Man, as the film still managed to eke out wins with the biggest preview sales of all time, and the biggest opening day sales of all time.

At just shy of $1 billion at the global box office, Spider-Man: Brand New Day could very well be the biggest earner of the year by the time 2026 ends. In this case (as well as many others), Marvel is likely its biggest competitor, with Avengers: Doomsday sure to have theaters swarming with moviegoers when its opening weekend arrives this December. Even then, either film could outperform the other when all is said and done as fans line up to catch the biggest reveals Marvel has to offer.

No matter how the future shakes out for Spidey, there was only one clear victor during the 2026 July-to-August weekend: movie fans. It was the biggest collective weekend in domestic box office history, reaching $430 million across the films available in theaters (via Variety).

Spider-Man: Brand New Day predictably made up the bulk of that number, with The Odyssey coming in second place at $51 million, Toy Story 5 in third with $6.3 million, Minions & Monsters in fourth with $5.8 million, and Disney's live-action Moana in fifth with $5.3 million. As the new animated Pixar film continues to build past the $1 billion milestone it reached last weekend, Christopher Nolan's epic adaptation is inching closer to it. The Odyssey now stands tall with $911.4 million worldwide as it continues to charge through expectations following its impressive debut.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day stars Holland, Zendaya, Sadie Sink, Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal, and more and picks up after the events of Spider-Man: No Way Home saw everyone on Earth lose their memories of Peter Parker. Despite just two movies on the calendar for 2026, the year could end up being one of Marvel Studios' biggest ever. We'll know if the new Spidey flick managed to secure a win over Endgame or get stuck in second in the coming days.

Until then, you can check out IGN's 7/10 review for the film. You can also check out what Metal Gear Solid creator Hideo Kojima thought about the movie, and you can learn about the leak the film got hit by on release day.

items.title: Hideo Kojima Reviews Spider-Man: Brand New Day: 'It Felt Fresh, and I Really Enjoyed It'
items.description: Movie critic Hideo Kojima has finally published his Spider-Man: Brand New Day review, and it turns out he "really enjoyed" its take on a "lonely Peter Parker."
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Movie critic Hideo Kojima has finally published his Spider-Man: Brand New Day review, and it turns out he "really enjoyed" its take on a "lonely Peter Parker."

The cinephile, who also happens to be the mind behind game franchises like Metal Gear Solid and Death Stranding, took to X/Twitter to unleash his thoughts on the latest Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) movie. Coming in at a little less than 200 words and 1000 characters, it's safe to say he found a lot to think about in Tom Holland's latest swing at Spidey.

"A lonely hero. A lonely Spidey. A lonely Peter Parker," Kojima said. "It felt fresh, and I really enjoyed it."

Followers know that Kojima will typically put a little extra thought into a longer review for movies that stuck with him, while the ones that didn't usually only get a sentence, if that. Spider-Man: Brand New Day falls into the first camp, with the review analyzing not only this weekend's box office hit but the MCU Spider-Man movies that have come before it, too.

"Until now, Spider-Man films have generally been grouped into self-contained trilogies," he continued. "With each new iteration, the cast and creative team changed, allowing the franchise to reinvent itself for a new era. This time, however, while both the cast and the story continue from the previous film, everything has been reset.

"The film focuses on Peter, once again alone, and the loneliness and inner conflict that come with that. It can be seen both as the beginning of a new series and as a direct continuation of the last one. A very clever structure."

Watched “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” A lonely hero. A lonely Spidey. A lonely Peter Parker. It felt fresh, and I really enjoyed it. Until now, Spider-Man films have generally been grouped into self-contained trilogies. With each new iteration, the cast and creative team changed,… pic.twitter.com/FSuLBVbnR0

— HIDEO_KOJIMA (@HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN) August 2, 2026

Kojima then took the opportunity to take a broader look at filmmaking on the scale of something like Spider-Man: Brand New Day. He added that "striking the right balance between what filmmakers want to create and what audiences expect has become incredibly difficult," especially as social media amplifies opinions online.

"Genuine, heartfelt filmmaking is becoming increasingly challenging. Because of that, this is a film that puts the 'Brand' in 'Brand New Day' to the test, as part of a blockbuster franchise that simply cannot afford to fail."

While fans wait for to hear more from new Kojima games like OD and Physint, the game creator has used social media to connect with followers online by sharing everything from community creations to the music he's been listening to. His movie reviews are no doubt the centerpiece of his activity, though. We've covered his thoughts on films like Backrooms and Superman before.

As audiences across the globe – Kojima included – head to theaters to check out the new MCU flick, you can see what IGN thought about it in our 7/10 Spider-Man: Brand New Day review. In it, we said the movie "effectively refocuses on the most reliable pillars of the webslinger: battling inner turmoil, swinging around NYC saving the day, and looking cool while doing so."

Photo by Rosdiana Ciaravolo/Getty Images.

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Beats Avengers: Endgame Record to Claim Biggest Domestic Opening Day of All Time
items.description: Marvel Studios' Spider-Man: Brand New Day has broken yet another record after webbing up a whopping $168 million at the domestic box office on its opening day.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Marvel Studios' Spider-Man: Brand New Day has broken yet another record after webbing up a whopping $168 million at the domestic box office on its opening day.

That's according to Variety, which reported that the latest Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) movie reached the figure on its July 31 premiere date. It's a number that gives it an $11 million lead over Avengers: Endgame's $157 million opening, securing its place as the film with the biggest opening day for a domestic release of all time.

Sony reportedly expects its Tom Holland-starring, Destin Daniel Cretton-directed Spider-Man: Brand New Day to accumulate $325 million by the weekend's end. Other estimates are said to be anticipating earnings to reach as high as $358 million. Should the latter pan out, it would also see the film beat Endgame's $357 million to nab the biggest domestic opening weekend of all time.

Seeing Spidey reach these heights is incredible but not out of character. Early expectations had the film poised for a massive debut. Preview audiences then helped the Marvel movie bring in $72 million, giving it not only a solid head start on the weekend but an additional broken record over Endgame's $60 million preview day.

Although we're only halfway through Spider-Man: Brand New Day's first weekend in theaters and global totals have yet to be tallied, it feels all but confirmed that it will manage to walk away with the biggest opening weekend of the year, if not of all time.

That's not to say Marvel hasn't had stiff competition in the lead-up to the release of its new summer blockbuster. Nintendo and Illumination's The Super Mario Galaxy Movie also had a strong opening in April and eventually went on to cross the $1 billion mark in June.

King of Pop biopic Michael pulled in record numbers upon its late April premiere and passed $1 billion last month, and Toy Story 5 piled on a global opening of $312 million in June before reaching $1 billion last weekend. Finally, there's The Odyssey, which exceeded expectations with its $264 million global opening. Although the Christopher Nolan movie hasn't reached the big B quite yet, it seems on track to sail past it in the near future. It looks like Spidey, meanwhile, will beat them all.

What Spider-Man: Brand New Day's finish will look like is anyone's guess, but it won't be long before we start talking about it passing that $1 billion milestone, too. While we wait for updates from the minds at Marvel, you can read IGN's 7/10 review. You can also read about a leak that hit the film yesterday, and how it teases a different take on one of the most iconic teams in comic book history.

items.title: Game of Thrones: The Mad King Reveals Full Stage Cast and First Portrait
items.description: See the first official cast photo for Game of Thrones: The Mad King stage play, featuring King Aerys II, Rhaegar Targaryen, Young Ned Stark, and more.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
The first photo and full cast for Game of Thrones: The Mad King was revealed Saturday by the Royal Shakespeare Company. The prequel stage show, announced in February, opens Saturday, August 8, at the Royal Shakespeare Theatre in Stratford-upon-Avon, England, and closes Saturday, September 5, 2026.

The release also marks the 30th anniversary of the original publication of George R. R. Martin’s A Game of Thrones, the first novel in the A Song of Ice and Fire series.

Adapted by Duncan Macmillan from Martin’s works and directed by Dominic Cooke, Game of Thrones: The Mad King spans “the final years before the events of the novels” and “reveals a legendary chapter of Westerosi history,” according to the official press release.

Left to right, the portrait includes Tanisha Spring as Ashara Dayne, Elizabeth Ayodele as Princess Elia Martell, Mariah Gayle as Queen Rhaella Targaryen, Callum Woodhouse as Lord Robert Baratheon, Michael Shaeffer as King Aerys II Targaryen, Harmony Rose-Bremner as Lyanna Stark, Luke Brady as Brandon Stark, Noah Ritter as Prince Rhaegar Targaryen and Michael Abubakar as Eddard Stark.

Here is the cast of George R. R. Martin’s Game of Thrones: The Mad King in alphabetical order:

Michael Abubakar (Eddard Stark), Elizabeth Ayodele (Princess Elia Martell), Maxim Ays (Ser Jaime Lannister), Miles Barrow (Benjen Stark), Islam Bouakkaz (Howland Reed), Luke Brady (Brandon Stark), Marty Breen (Catelyn Stark), Sebastian Charles (Owen Merryweather / Ensemble / Puppeteer), Adrian Christopher (Prince Lewyn Martell / Ensemble / Puppeteer), Ronan Cullen (On-stage Swing / Puppeteer), Fred Davis (Qarlton Chelsted / Maester / Ensemble / Puppeteer), Edem-Ita Duke (Oberyn Martell), Simi Egbejumi-David (Ensemble / Puppeteer), Daisy Franks (Cersei Lannister / Golda Whent / Ensemble / Puppeteer), Mariah Gale (Queen Rhaella Targaryen / Lady Shella Whent), Richard Hansell (Grand Maester Pycelle), Daniel Hawksford (Ser Barristan Selmy), Lewis Howard (Ensemble / Puppeteer), April Nerissa Hudson (Ensemble / Puppeteer), Tom Larkin (Lord Whent / Wisdom Rossart / Ensemble / Puppeteer), Chelsea Marie (Ensemble / Puppeteer), Kel Matsena (Ser Arthur Dayne), Shaun Yusuf McKee (Ser Gerold Hightower / Ensemble / Puppeteer), Alexander Newland (Lord Rickard Stark), Hughie O’Donnell (Lord Varys), Huw Parmenter (Ser Oswell Whent), Noah Ritter (Prince Rhaegar Targaryen), Harmony Rose-Bremner (Lyanna Stark), Kate Rowsell (On-stage Swing / Puppeteer), Michael Shaeffer (King Aerys II Targaryen), Tanisha Spring (Ashara Dayne), Tom Stacy (On-stage Swing / Puppeteer), Matt Tait (Ensemble / Puppeteer), Tzarina-Nassor (Ensemble / Puppeteer), Marcello Walton (Ser Jonothor Darry / Lord Tywin Lannister) and Callum Woodhouse (Lord Robert Baratheon).

In addition to Dominic and Duncan, the play’s creative team are Puppetry and Movement Nick Barnes and Finn Caldwell (Lume); Set Designer Chloe Lamford; Costume Designer Georgia McGuinness; Lighting Designer Jon Clark; Composer Will Stuart; Sound Designer Tom Gibbons; Casting Director Amy Ball CDG; Fight Director Bethan Clark; Intimacy Director Ingrid Mackinnon; Voice & Text Jeannette Nelson; Dialect Hazel Holder; Associate Director Emily Raymond; Associate Puppetry and Movement Scarlet Wilderink; Period Dance Consultant Francesca Roche; Creative Consultant Ti Mikkel; Director’s Consultant Lenore Gallegos; Associate Puppetry Designer Oli Simonon; Associate Set Designer Machiko Weston; Associate Costume Designer Alex Berry; Associate Lighting Designer Lucía Sánchez Roldan; Associate Sound Designer Alex Twiselton and Assistant Director Bellaray Bertrand-Webb.

Game of Thrones: The Mad King is co-produced with Simon Painter, Tim Lawson, Mark Manuel, Warner Bros. Theatre Ventures, HBO and Sir Leonard Blavatnik and Danny Cohen for Access Entertainment.

items.title: Vincent Pastore, The Sopranos Actor, Dies at 80
items.description: Vincent Pastore, the actor best known for playing Salvatore Bonpensiero in the groundbreaking TV series The Sopranos, has died at 80.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Vincent Pastore, the actor best known for playing Salvatore Bonpensiero in the groundbreaking TV series The Sopranos, has died at 80.

The actor was found dead in his home in the Bronx today, August 1, as reported by Deadline. A neighbor reportedly discovered his body while checking on him after he hadn't been heard from for three days.

items.title: Elden Ring Players Are Hoping for Godwyn DLC After FromSoftware Shares Cryptic Social Media Post
items.description: It's been two years since FromSoftware released its Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, but a new post from the developer has some fans believing that even more Elden Ring DLC is on the way.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
It's been two years since FromSoftware released its Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, but a new post from the developer has some fans believing that even more Elden Ring DLC is on the way.

Outside of a few updates for multiplayer spinoff Nightreign and A24's live-action movie, things have been quiet over in the Elden Ring camp. So, when the studio behind the critically acclaimed fantasy RPG franchise published a somewhat ambiguous social media post, fans wasted no time going rabid with excitement.

"Even the perilous hunt for the demigods holds moments of quiet wonder," the X/Twitter post said, accompanying a 12-second video of a player riding through Siofra River.

Even the perilous hunt for the demigods holds moments of quiet wonder.#ELDENRING pic.twitter.com/5sJyVOYi17

— ELDEN RING (@ELDENRING) July 31, 2026

It's innocuous enough on its own, but for those who have waited years for more Elden Ring DLC, it's turned into a gold mine to spin theories off of. The post itself has racked up 4.8 million views and 17.4K likes at the time of this piece's publication, with its replies filled with those who believe FromSoftware is trying to very, very subtly tell players that something is coming.

"GODWYN DLC?????" one popular quote post said.

"I am delusional please give me a second expansion," another said.

It's true that this post is a bit different from the studio's usual activity. The Elden Ring social media feed has been known to be either very direct, sharing things like announcements for updates, or extremely vague. Even then, it's hard to find a post quite like the one that has fans riled up, with few similar messages throughout 2025, if at all.

More Elden Ring dlc????! pic.twitter.com/bPjlNekm7J

— Kaida 🌊 (@khaliltooshort) July 31, 2026

FROMSOFT RELEASE GODWYN DLC AND MY LIFE IS YOURS pic.twitter.com/QSKmuNhuoh

— The Particle of God (@Vinicus1013) August 1, 2026

> HUNT for the DEMIGODS
> shows empty siofra river
> one way to get to deeproot depths is through the siofra aqueduct and transporter coffin
> GODWYN DLC ????? https://t.co/h8qZ6OU4Da

— jar saint (@scadutree) August 1, 2026

The video being set in Siofra River and the lack of giant crab and Ancestral Follower enemies also have players on edge for more Elden Ring DLC. Unfortunately, there is very little concrete evidence suggesting another expansion is on the way, at least for right now.

Besides the post itself mostly seeming to highlight one of Elden Ring's many standout moments, there are plenty of other things it could be building hype toward. The team behind the Elden Ring movie announced they had wrapped filming earlier this week ahead of its March 3, 2028, release date, for example. Our money, however, is on the Tarnished Edition that is set to come to Nintendo Switch 2 in just a few weeks.

FromSoftware is no doubt interested in pushing fans to check it and its new content out, even if it is insubstantial compared to something like Shadow of the Erdtree. Some fans have also pointed out that the video seems to feature one of Torrent's new skins, which will also be available on other platforms in the near future.

I JUST REALIZED THAT'S ONE OF THE NEW TORRENT SKINS IN THE VIDEO https://t.co/h8qZ6OU4Da pic.twitter.com/dOJ4JPp5LP

— jar saint (@scadutree) August 1, 2026

The only thing Elden Ring fans know they can look forward to in the next month is the Tarnished Edition, but that isn't stopping fans from showing up in droves to plead with FromSoftware to release another DLC expansion. There are also those showing up in the replies section to call for more content for Nightreign, while those hoping for base game DLC argue they'd rather FromSoftware return to the game that started the franchise back in 2022.

Then, of course, there are the Bloodborne fans. Poor things.

For now, FromSoftware has not confirmed a second major DLC expansion for Elden Ring. We do know that the studio has some things in development, but outside of previously announced projects like The Duskbloods, much of its future remains a mystery.

IGN called Elden Ring a "Masterpiece" in our original 10/10 review. The Shadow of the Erdtree DLC earned the same rating.

items.title: Barbie 2 Will Have to Start from Scratch if Warner Bros. Can't Make a Deal With Talent by December
items.description: Negotiations for Barbie 2 have come to a halt, and if Warner Bros. can't make a deal by December 2026, it will lose director Greta Gerwig, writer Noah Baumbach, and stars Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Negotiations for Barbie 2 have come to a halt, and if Warner Bros. can't make a deal by December 2026, it will lose director Greta Gerwig, writer Noah Baumbach, and stars Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling.

A behind-the-scenes update on the sequel to 2023's box office success was shared in a new report from The New York Times. Three years removed from its theatrical premiere, one would expect progress on a sequel to be further along, but it sounds like Warner Bros. and the talent behind the first film are locked in a monthslong standoff.

It's said that both parties have failed to agree to a deal to see the cast and crew return for Barbie 2 after the first film managed to bring in a record-breaking $1.5 billion in theaters (via Box Office Mojo). Warner Bros.'s offers to the returning talent include a cut of box office profits based on its success, as well as raises, including paying Gosling his $20 million asking price. The site's sources stated that current Warner Bros. CEO David Zaslav believes the offers on the table are "too generous" and refused to give them the OK.

A Warner Bros. representative refuted that claim, saying instead that talent representatives declined an offer made in May and have yet to file a counteroffer. As Barbie 2 floats in limbo, the report noted that time is not on anyone's side.

Should a deal fail to be reached by December, rights to the movie franchise will revert back to Mattel. Although that could still eventually see a second live-action Barbie movie materialize at another studio, it would do so without Gerwig, Baumbach, Robbie, or Gosling. It would also be required to proceed without carrying over any of the story elements established in the 2023 project.

"We have a rights deal with Mattel in place and have made a series of big offers to try and finalize deals to make the next Barbie film," Warner Bros. co-chairs Pam Abdy and Michael De Luca said in a joint statement. "Unfortunately, we have been unable to reach an agreement thus far."

It's hard to imagine what Barbie would have looked like without the creative team behind it. The movie premiered not only to success at the box office but rave reviews praising it as an imaginative take on a decades-old IP.

Gerwig told Deadline in March 2024 that she had come around on the idea of a Barbie sequel, saying, "I want to do it." Even then, it was clear the wait for more would be long, as both Robbie and the creative team had previously said their expectations to deliver a Barbie 2 were low.

Gerwig and Baumbach have reportedly expressed they already have a story for Barbie 2 in mind and are ready to begin the writing process. That, of course, won't happen until a deal is made. With progress now at a standstill, it could still be years before another movie is made, and that's if Warner Bros. and the talent are even able to come to an agreement.

For now, Barbie exists as a standalone movie. IGN gave it a 9/10 review, calling it "a masterful exploration of femininity and the pressures of perfection."

items.title: Palworld TCG Prices Skyrocket as eBay Scalpers Profit Off of Card Game Launch
items.description: The Palworld TCG has officially launched, and so too has a wave of scalpers looking to make a quick buck on developer Pocketpair's new collectible cards.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
The Palworld TCG has officially launched, and so too has a wave of scalpers looking to make a quick buck on developer Pocketpair's new collectible cards.

As promised back in January, the developer has partnered with Bushiroad to deliver an official Palworld trading card game and released its first wave of cards, Dawn of Palpagos July 30, 2026. It was an announcement that predictably triggered further comparisons to Pokémon, and also like the original pocket monster property, Pocketpair's latest creation has some people selling cards for hundreds or even thousands of dollars.

As spotted by GamesRadar, eBay has filled with both successful and ongoing listings for everything from booster box cases to, of course, individual (and extremely rare) cards. For reference, retailer Lumius was selling a booster box case – which comes with 12 booster boxes that carry 12 booster packs each – for $499.99. Cases are going for about $1,800 on eBay.

While there are plenty of Palworld fans clearly looking to collect their favorite Pals simply for the love of the game, scalpers online have a different plan. Some buyers who lucked out and got their purchases shipped early had already posted listings for cards before that official July 30 launch date.

One Cattiva Gold Soul Card, which appears to be the rarest of the collection so far, seemingly sold for an unbelievable $3,997.98 three days early on July 27. A Jormuntide Ignis card sold for $1,300 even earlier on July 24. While cases are hovering at around $1,800 on eBay post-Palworld TCG launch, a master case containing three regular cases sold for $5,990 just 24 hours after launch.

These prices are nothing new to Pokémon fans, but it doesn't make seeing them pop up online so quickly sting any less. Successful prices do seem to have come down in the few days since collectors and scalpers started receiving their orders, with those Gold Cattiva Pals now seemingly going for around $1,000 each.

Palworld OFFICIAL CARD GAME is officially launched and NOW ON SALE! 🎉🔥

Available now with a worldwide simultaneous release in English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese! 🌎

Begin your journey with Trial Decks and power up your builds with cards from the Booster Pack in the… pic.twitter.com/1Y6gCvTsGB

— Palworld OFFICIAL CARD GAME (@PalworldOCG_EN) July 30, 2026

Pocketpair seems to have gotten off to a roaring start with its Palworld TCG despite the obvious comparisons being lobbed its way. July 9, weeks before launch, the company reported it had achieved 3.5 million packs ordered. The Dawn of Palpagos set features more than 50 Pals with original illustrations, with a second booster set, Legends Awaken, set to follow this October. For more on the latest collectible trading card game to sweep gamers off their feet, you can read everything you need to know about Palworld TCG.

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Leak on Social Media Reportedly Seen by Millions Before Sony Took It Down
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day has reportedly suffered a significant leak that saw a high-quality bootleg spread across X/Twitter before Sony took it down.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day has reportedly suffered a significant leak that saw a high-quality bootleg spread across X/Twitter before Sony took it down.

It's yet another leak in X's lineup that arrived just as Tom Holland's latest go at the Wall-Crawler swung into cinemas, according to Variety. The site stated that user Fredrick Bryan posted the movie earlier today, leaving users to view the film and reveal its biggest surprises for hours before Sony was able to take it down.

It's reported the post reached 5.9 million X accounts, accumulated more than 143,000 likes, and passed 10,000 reshares. IGN hasn't been able to find any reuploads of the movie on social media yet, but traces can still be found if you know where to look.

"DUDE NO I WAS WATCHING THIS SPIDERMAN BRAND NEW DAY MOVIE ON TWITTER AND IT SUDDENLY STOPPED PLAYING," one user said.

"Yo did anybody download that Spider-Man Brand New Day movie that just dropped? I forgot to download it before it got deleted," another user said with "loudly crying face" emojis.

Short segments revealing some of Spider-Man: Brand New Day's biggest reveals also started floating around on X. While some of those posts remain online, a message saying "this media has been disabled in response to a report by the copyright owner" can now be found in the video's place. Some users still have posts available stating they saw at least the first chunk of the movie before it was removed, while others say they were able to nearly finish it.

As the leak made its way online and was promptly removed, Marvel Studios has unfortunately followed in the footsteps of Christopher Nolan and his new movie, The Odyssey. A high-quality rip featuring all three hours of that film was posted on X last weekend, giving millions of users the opportunity to watch it or at least get a taste of what it's like instead of going to the theaters to watch it. While Sony told Variety it had no comment regarding its leak, Universal did share its own statement.

"We became aware of the unauthorized posting of the film and immediately initiated takedown protocols," Universal told Variety in a statement. "We take copyright infringement seriously and will pursue all appropriate remedies to protect our content and intellectual property rights."

It's unclear if Sony has any plans to take further action regarding the Spider-Man: Brand New Day leaks on X. For now, the film has only just been released in theaters today, July 31, 2026.

IGN gave Holland's latest swing a 7/10 review. The film brought in an incredible $72 million in box office previews, though how exactly it will fare throughout its opening weekend remains to be seen. Meanwhile, Sony has already been doing its best to combat leaks related to its post-credits scene.

"Yo did anybody download that Spider-Man Brand New Day movie that just dropped? I forgot to download it before it got deleted," another user said with "loudly crying face" emojis.

Short segments revealing some of Spider-Man: Brand New Day's biggest reveals also started floating around on X. While some of those posts remain online, a message saying "this media has been disabled in response to a report by the copyright owner" can now be found in the video's place. Some users still have posts available stating they saw at least the first chunk of the movie before it was removed, while others say they were able to nearly finish it.

"We became aware of the unauthorized posting of the film and immediately initiated takedown protocols," Universal told Variety in a statement. "We take copyright infringement seriously and will pursue all appropriate remedies to protect our content and intellectual property rights."

It's unclear if Sony has any plans to take further action regarding the Spider-Man: Brand New Day leaks on X. For now, the film has only just been released in theaters today, July 31, 2026.

IGN gave Holland's latest swing a 7/10 review. The film brought in an incredible $72 million in box office previews, though how exactly it will fare throughout its opening weekend remains to be seen. Meanwhile, Sony has already been doing its best to combat leaks related to its post-credits scene.

items.title: Booster Gold TV Show Writer Says His DC Series 'Won't Be Moving Forward'
items.description: It's a sad day for superhero fans, as just hours after actor Mahershala Ali announced he's no longer working on Marvel's Blade, writer David Jenkins confirmed his Booster Gold TV show also "won't be moving forward."
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
UPDATE 1:35pm PT: Just as Jenkins announced his Booster Gold show would not be moving forward, The Wrap reported that development on the project will move forward with a new creative team.

DC Studios will reportedly continue to attempt to get Booster Gold on its feet without the Our Flag Means Death creator, though who may be involved remains a mystery. It was also stated that a lead actor has yet to be cast.

Booster Gold remains without a release date. Losing Jenkins suggests it could be a while before we see the project come to be.

ORIGINAL: It's a sad day for superhero fans, as just hours after actor Mahershala Ali announced he's no longer working on Marvel's Blade, writer David Jenkins confirmed his Booster Gold TV show also "won't be moving forward."

The Our Flag Means Death creator offered an unceremonious conclusion for his long-in-development series adaptation with a post on Threads. It's an announcement that followed months of speculation that the project's demise was near, with Jenkins pointing to Ali's cancelation confirmation as a good example for his feelings.

For now, it's unclear if the project as a whole is dead, or if only Jenkins' version of the show has come to an end. At the very least, it seems like quite the setback for the DCU.

"My Booster Gold won't be moving forward," he said. "Can't improve on Mahershala's lovely statement so I'll just apply it here as well."

Although it's unclear if it could materialize in the future, it seems to be curtains for yet another big superhero project. Jenkins doesn't think he could have shared the news any better than Ali, who confirmed his Blade movie for the Marvel Cinematic Universe had taken a stake through the heart.

"For whatever reason, that project is not for me," the segment from Ali's interview with GQ before it was shared by Jenkins said. "If they wanted to do it, we would've done it. So I have to move on, and I have moved on.

"Again, you had me under contract, they have billions of dollars, if they wanted to do the movie, we would've done the movie. I feel ready to move on from the Blade questions. Those questions are for them. They didn't want to do it, so they should answer that question.

DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn previously announced his plan to bring a live-action story based on the witty time traveler during an all-encompassing DCU reveal video back in 2023. It was a moment that had fans hopeful for the future of the company's movie ambitions, but in the years since, we've heard crushingly little about the project.

"Booster Gold is one of comics' really popular cult heroes," Gunn promised at the time. "He is a fascinating guy. He's a loser from the future who uses future technology to come back to the present day and become a superhero, so that people will love him. It is basically the superhero story of imposter syndrome on an HBO Max series."

Gunn then said Booster Gold was "going pretty strong" in February 2025 before Jenkins signed on to handle the pilot the following July. At the time, it was reported that, should the show get the full series treatment, Jenkins would be its showrunner.

Gunn eventually gave an update on Booster Gold in April of this year, saying simply the series was still "in development." He confirmed another DC show, Paradise Lost, was also "in extreme development," while also revealing that The Authority project had been paused and could show up "maybe some day" but "not soon." Jenkins then published a post confirming he had turned in his pilot script in June.

Next up on the DCU slate is Lanterns, which premieres in August. Clayface will then bring the comic book universe back to the big screen when it arrives in October. The budding cinematic universe had struggled in recent months after Supergirl failed to perform in theaters, but with Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow still set for next year, it's clear Gunn and company are just getting started.

media:description.$text: As a time-travelling man on a mission, Booster Gold is the only hero apart from Barry Allen who recognizes that time has gone horribly awry in Flashpoint. Booster does his best to restore the true timeline during the Flashpoint conflict, but he's sidetracked by a feud with Captain Nathaniel Adam and his pet monstrosity, Doomsday. Booster eventually returns home to the Vanishing Point, but unlike Barry he loses all memory of Flashpoint in the process.

items.title: Obsession Star Inde Navarrette Wants to Play Mystique Following Talks With X-Men Director
items.description: Obsession star Inde Navarrette has named Mystique as the character she wants to play in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) following talks with X-Men director Jake Schreier.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Obsession star Inde Navarrette has named Mystique as the character she wants to play in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) following talks with X-Men director Jake Schreier.

The breakout star from May's low-budget horror hit confirmed she met with the filmmaker at least once during a recent interview with Variety. It's a meeting she's mentioned before, and while she refrained from spilling the beans about everything they talked about, it sounds like her potential future in the MCU is something that's still on her mind.

A segment from her conversation with the site saw the actress picking common Google searches featuring her name from a fish bowl. When one search said, "Inde Navarrette Black Cat," she confessed she didn't know who the Spider-Man character is. Still, the online chatter from fans hoping to see her join the MCU in some capacity is something she's keenly aware of.

"Every time that I see something like this I'll giggle because, like, obviously I know the truth, but I would love to be a part of Marvel," Navarrette said. "I think it's fun, especially since I grew up watching X-Men – the 2000 X-Men. That would be fun."

When pressed on her meeting with Schreier, she clarified that she's been taking "a lot of meetings" since Obsession crept its way into theaters earlier this year. That could mean a lot of things, but at least as far as the MCU is concerned, she's happy to sing the director's praises.

"I thought what he brought to Thunderbolts* was what I used to love about Marvel. It was character-driven," Navarrette added. "So, the whole time, I just couldn't stop yappin' about how much I appreciated what he had brought to Marvel.

"That's the luxury that I have right now, meeting all of these different kinds of people. Not all of them turn into projects. It'll be, 'I just really want to work with you, and I've seen this project of yours and this and this and this.' So, I just really wanted to congratulate him on bringing back my favorite thing of Thunderbolts*, and he's a very sweet person."

Even if her meeting with Schreier did get her foot in the door at Marvel HQ, it seems she's not ready to confirm any casting news yet. It makes sense, especially as the MCU drip feeds fans updates, including today's, which saw Ready or Not star Samara Weaving confirmed to play Emma Frost. Navarrette does, however, have one character in mind, should she get the call.

"Oh, I mean, Mystique has always been super cool," she replied when asked who she'd like to play. "Growing up, I remember watching the behind-the-scenes process of all the prosthetics. That was super cool for me. I would always watch behind-the-scenes of a lot of stuff. Pirates of the Caribbean, I remember, was a big thing that I would watch the BTS of. X-Men, you know, the prosthetics. I just find it so fascinating."

Hearing Navarrette shout out Mystique might sound like music to the ears of those who have been campaigning to see her play the mutant shapeshifter. Again, nothing is confirmed quite yet, but as Marvel continues tracking down younger talent to fill the roles of the X-Men, anything is possible. For now, it is at least confirmed that 2000s Mystique actress Rebecca Romijn will return alongside her X-Men co-stars in Avengers: Doomsday later this year.

As we wait to see how Navarrette follows up Obsession, you can check out IGN's Spider-Man: Brand New Day review. You can also see how she reacted to a fan gifting her a rare copy of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2.
